efficacy.note: Whole-body Gcgr deletion lowered fed and fasted glucose and improved oral glucose tolerance; the genetic ceiling for antagonist efficacy, no patient comparison yet.
efficacy.quote: Blood glucose levels were somewhat reduced in GR(-/-) mice relative to wild type, in both the fed and fasted state.
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level. First Gcgr-/- report (BBRC, January 2002); Gelling 2003 (doi:10.1073/pnas.0237106100) is the fuller characterisation. No FDA review exists for any member, so model_filed is null.
efficacy.judgement: Opening entry at the knockout's first use. The system is the genetic counterpart of full receptor antagonism, not a dosed model, so no member compound can be in it (product_in_model false) and no dose entry is possible.

efficacy.note: LY2409021 cut HbA1c 0.65-0.83% at 12 weeks, the direction the knockout's lower glucose and STZ-resistance predicted; MK-3577 and PF-06291874 replicated.
efficacy.short: HbA1c fell as the knockout predicted
efficacy.quote: After 12 weeks, least squares (LS) mean change from baseline in HbA1c was -0.83% (10 mg), -0.65% (30 mg), and -0.66% (60 mg) (all P < 0.05) vs. placebo, 0.11%.
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level, paywalled; drafter's pairing of the knockout (Conarello 2007 as the diabetic-setting model side: 'Gcgr (-/-) mice were resistant to STZ-induced hyperglycaemia') with the first member Phase 2. Online 2015-12-17, print 2016; registry results for NCT00871572 and NCT01241448 both posted 2018-04-24.
efficacy.judgement: Same, direction only: a lifelong knockout cannot give an effect size for a 12-week drug trial. Dated to the first member efficacy result (Kazda 2016), not to the earlier non-member MK-0893 Phase 2.

patient_trials.quote: LY2409021 produced reductions in HbA1c that were significantly different from placebo over both 12 and 24 weeks.

safety.note: Knockout predicted ~100-fold hyperglucagonaemia with near-normal glycaemia and normal lipids; alpha-cell hyperplasia (Gelling 2003), PNETs (Yu 2011) and 'adverse lipid changes' (Yang 2011) followed.
safety.quote: Plasma glucagon levels were strikingly elevated in both fed and fasted animals.
safety.confidence_note: Abstract-level. The track's later predictions, all before any member patient result: alpha-cell hyperplasia (Gelling 2003, doi:10.1073/pnas.0237106100), lean and steatosis-resistant on high-fat diet (Conarello 2007, doi:10.1007/s00125-006-0481-3), raised hepatic triglyceride secretion on fasting (Longuet 2008, doi:10.1016/j.cmet.2008.09.008), PNETs by 10-12 months (Yu 2011, doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0023397), raised plasma amino acids, cholesterol and bile acids with 'adverse lipid changes' (Yang 2011, doi:10.1186/1471-2164-12-281).
safety.judgement: Opening entry. Modality left null: every harm the knockout can speak to is on-target, which the brief pools across modalities.

safety.note: 28-day LY2409021 raised glucagon and lowered glucose with minimal hypoglycaemia in T2D, as the knockout's hyperglucagonaemia-without-hypoglycaemia predicted; alpha-cell hyperplasia not assessable.
safety.quote: Fasting and postprandial glucose were reduced and glucagon levels increased after single and multiple dosing, with reductions in fasting serum glucose of up to ∼1.25 mmol/l on day 28.
safety.confidence_note: Abstract-level, paywalled; drafter's pairing with Gelling 2003. Kelly 2015 gives no glucagon fold-change, so magnitude is direction only (the knockout's two-orders-of-magnitude rise is far larger than any dosed-human value). The 28-day study NCT01606397 posted no results.
safety.judgement: Same on the knockout's first stated harm (hyperglucagonaemia) and on its glycaemic safety (near-normal glycaemia, 'minimal hypoglycaemia'). The transaminase rise is not charged here: the knockout papers reported no liver enzymes in their abstracts, and a knockout characterisation is not a toxicology screen; its stated predictions govern.

safety.note: PF-06291874 raised LDL-C and gluconeogenic amino acids in T2D, the 'adverse lipid changes' and hyperaminoacidaemia Yang 2011 read off the knockout liver five years earlier.
safety.short: Knockout's lipid and amino-acid warning held
safety.quote: Small dose-dependent increases in LDL cholesterol were observed, along with reversible increases in serum aminotransferases that were largely within the laboratory reference range.
safety.confidence_note: Abstract-level, paywalled; drafter's pairing with Yang 2011 ('increased amino acids, cholesterol, and bile acid levels ... may be associated with adverse lipid changes', online 2011-06-01). Online 2016-05-12; NCT01856595 results posted 2018-11-01. Kazierad 2016 also reports 'An increase in circulating gluconeogenic amino acids was also observed on days 2 and 14.'
safety.judgement: Strengthens the match with a prospective prediction the dosed-animal packages did not make: the knockout polyomics named cholesterol and amino acids as the liabilities of full antagonism before any member reported them. Kazda 2017 and Guzman 2017 later reproduced the lipid rise with LY2409021.
safety.magnitude_basis: direction of plasma cholesterol and amino-acid change

safety.note: Six months of LY2409021 raised liver fat 4.4%, ALT, weight and blood pressure in T2D; the high-fat-fed knockout was lean and steatosis-resistant, the opposite prediction.
safety.short: Patients gained fat and weight; knockout lean
safety.quote: LY2409021 was also associated with significant increases in systolic blood pressure vs sitagliptin (4.9 mm Hg; P = .030) and vs placebo (4.3 mm Hg; P = .029), as well as significant increases in body weight and total cholesterol.
safety.confidence_note: Abstract-level, paywalled; drafter's pairing with Conarello 2007 ('decreased body weight and food intake ... resistant to the development of hepatic steatosis' on high-fat diet). Online 2017-06-08; NCT02111096 (terminated, n=174) results posted 2018-04-24. Hepatic fat fraction +4.44% vs placebo and ALT +10.7 U/L are in the same abstract.
safety.reason: Weight and liver fat went the other way
safety.judgement: Contra, magnitude opposite: on body weight and liver fat the knockout predicted the wrong direction for the setting closest to T2D patients (high-fat-fed), and one wrong prediction beats the same-track matches on glucagon and cholesterol. Longuet 2008 (fasting raised hepatic triglyceride secretion) points the other way, so the liver-fat call rests on the fed phenotype; weight is unambiguous. Blood pressure, never a knockout readout, is neither credited nor charged; PNETs (Yu 2011) are untestable in six-month trials. The track cannot turn back without a tier 1-4 source showing the harms attenuated.
safety.magnitude_basis: direction of body weight and hepatic fat change

added_models.model: Mahvash disease: homozygous GCGR loss-of-function in humans

safety.model: Mahvash disease: homozygous GCGR loss-of-function in humans
safety.note: First human homozygous GCGR loss-of-function (P86S): marked hyperglucagonaemia, alpha-cell hyperplasia and an islet tumour without glucagonoma syndrome; the human-genetic read-out of lifelong antagonism.
safety.short: Human GCGR loss: hyperglucagonaemia, islet tumour
safety.quote: We hereby report the first homozygous missense mutation in the human GCGR, which is associated with alpha cell hyperplasia and hyperglucagonemia.
safety.confidence_note: Open access (PMC2767399), abstract-level reading. Print 2009-11, no earlier online date in Europe PMC. Yu 2011 (doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0023397) adds that the same patient 'further develops pancreatic neuroendocrine tumors'.
safety.judgement: Opening entry at the first case. A single patient with a lifelong loss of function; no drug is in the system, so product_in_model is false and dose does not apply.

safety.model: Mahvash disease: homozygous GCGR loss-of-function in humans
safety.note: GRA-dosed T2D patients showed the Mahvash hyperglucagonaemia within 28 days with minimal hypoglycaemia; alpha-cell hyperplasia and PNET risk cannot show in short trials.
safety.quote: Fasting and postprandial glucose were reduced and glucagon levels increased after single and multiple dosing, with reductions in fasting serum glucose of up to ∼1.25 mmol/l on day 28.
safety.confidence_note: Abstract-level, paywalled; drafter's pairing with Zhou 2009. The 28-day study NCT01606397 posted no results. A second human loss-of-function case (Larger 2016, doi:10.1530/EDM-16-0081, online 2016-11-21) adds hyperaminoacidaemia and no hypoglycaemia, after Kazierad 2016 had already reported the amino-acid rise with PF-06291874, so it changes no status.
safety.judgement: Same, direction only, on the one Mahvash feature a drug trial can reach (hyperglucagonaemia). Not charged for silence on transaminases, lipids or blood pressure: a single case report is not a negative screen, and PNET, the harm this system uniquely predicts, is untestable in trials of six months. Prediction level stays class; Mahvash does not select responders.

added_models.model: GRA-dosed mouse LDL-C / cholesterol-absorption model (MK-0893 and structurally diverse GRAs)

safety.model: GRA-dosed mouse LDL-C / cholesterol-absorption model (MK-0893 and structurally diverse GRAs)
safety.note: Mice dosed with MK-0893 and other GRAs raised LDL-C through GLP-2-linked cholesterol absorption, abolished by ezetimibe; predicts an on-target LDL-C rise for every antagonist.
safety.short: Mouse traces GRA LDL-C to absorption
safety.quote: To examine potential pharmacologic mitigation, coadministration of ezetimibe (a potent inhibitor of cholesterol absorption) in mice abrogated the GRA-associated increase of LDL-c.
safety.confidence_note: Open access (PMC4617405) but the full-text fetch returned nothing, so abstract-level: the 'structurally diverse GRAs' are not named and none is known to be a member (product_in_model false). Online 2015-09-15, print 2015-11.
safety.judgement: Opening entry. The model was built to explain MK-0893's human LDL-C rise, a non-member result, so that retrodiction is not scored; its member predictions from 2015-09-15 onward are prospective (decision 10). Modality null: the mechanism is on-target, so the harm pools across antibody and small molecule.

safety.model: GRA-dosed mouse LDL-C / cholesterol-absorption model (MK-0893 and structurally diverse GRAs)
safety.note: PF-06291874, a member the model never saw, raised LDL-C dose-dependently in T2D within 14-28 days, as the cholesterol-absorption mouse predicted.
safety.short: LDL-C rise appeared with first member
safety.quote: Small dose-dependent increases in LDL cholesterol were observed, along with reversible increases in serum aminotransferases that were largely within the laboratory reference range.
safety.confidence_note: Abstract-level, paywalled; drafter's pairing. Online 2016-05-12, eight months after the model; NCT01856595 results posted 2018-11-01. No member LDL-C datum was found public before 2015-09-15 (Kelly 2015 and Kazda 2016 abstracts report none), but a conference abstract could not be excluded.
safety.judgement: Prospective same for the class: the first member LDL-C report post-dates the model. Direction only; neither abstract gives a comparable LDL-C magnitude.

safety.model: GRA-dosed mouse LDL-C / cholesterol-absorption model (MK-0893 and structurally diverse GRAs)
safety.note: Six weeks of LY2409021 20 mg raised serum lipids in 270 T2D patients at a dose that lowered HbA1c; second member, same on-target lipid rise.
safety.quote: Statistically significant increases in BP, MAP and serum lipid levels were observed with LY2409021 treatment at a dose that lowered HbA1c and glucose levels.
safety.confidence_note: Abstract-level, paywalled; drafter's pairing. Online 2017-03-27; NCT02091362 results posted 2018-07-19. Guzman 2017 (doi:10.1111/dom.12958) adds total cholesterol at six months.

safety.model: GRA-dosed mouse LDL-C / cholesterol-absorption model (MK-0893 and structurally diverse GRAs)
safety.note: Twelve weeks of the antibody volagidemab raised LDL-C in T1D: the harm follows the target, not the chemotype, as cholesterol absorption implies. Imported from T1D.
safety.quote: No increase in hypoglycemia was observed with volagidemab therapy; however, increases in serum transaminases, low-density lipoprotein (LDL)-cholesterol and blood pressure were observed.
safety.confidence_note: Imported from T1D (NCT03117998, results posted 2023-05-25); abstract-level. Online 2022-10-03.
safety.reason: LDL-C rise held for three members
safety.judgement: Strengthens with a third member and the other modality; safety comparisons transfer across indications (imported_from MONDO:0005147).

added_models.model: Semi-mechanistic glucose-to-HbA1c models (ADOPT, FFH, FHH, IGRH) fitted to LY2409021 Phase 1b

efficacy.model: Semi-mechanistic glucose-to-HbA1c models (ADOPT, FFH, FHH, IGRH) fitted to LY2409021 Phase 1b
efficacy.note: Four semi-mechanistic HbA1c models built on 4-week LY2409021 PK, glucose and HbA1c data to project 24-week HbA1c before the comparison is made.
efficacy.quote: The models were built using LY2409021 pharmacokinetics, glucose, and HbA1c data from a 4-week Phase 1b study.
efficacy.judgement: Opening entry at the model's first use; the comparison is in the same paper. Built in 2025 on a programme that stopped in 2017, so it is a retrodiction by construction.

efficacy.model: Semi-mechanistic glucose-to-HbA1c models (ADOPT, FFH, FHH, IGRH) fitted to LY2409021 Phase 1b
efficacy.note: FHH and IGRH models reproduced the 24-week Phase 2b HbA1c fall within 0.1%; ADOPT and FFH over-predicted by 0.29% and 0.15%.
efficacy.quote: Overall, the FHH and IGRH models closely predicted the mean ΔHbA1c at Week 24 within 0.1% difference from the observed values in the Phase 2b study.
efficacy.confidence_note: Open access, abstract-level. The 24-week Phase 2b is NCT01241448 (LY2409021 2.5-20 mg, Kazda 2016), results posted 2018-04-24. Two of the four candidate models over-predicted; the source calls the transit-compartment models the match.
efficacy.judgement: Retro, not same: the 24-week result was published in 2015 and the models were evaluated against it in 2025. Within 2x on the stated quantity (mean change in HbA1c at week 24). Class-level: it predicts the regimen's HbA1c, not which patients respond. A dose entry is not opened because the paper chose no human dose.
efficacy.magnitude_basis: mean change in HbA1c at week 24, model-estimated vs observed

considered_not_added: Anti-GCGR mAb / Gcgr-/- hepatic amino-acid axis models with human islets (Solloway 2015 doi:10.1016/j.celrep.2015.06.034; Dean 2017 doi:10.1016/j.cmet.2017.05.011): the amino-acid rise they predict appeared with PF-06291874 (Kazierad 2016), but the dosed system is the draft's existing antibody-in-mouse track (strengthens it, not a new model_id) and the knockout arm is folded into gcgr-ko-mouse; alpha-cell endpoints are unassessable in patients

GCGR antisense oligonucleotide in db/db mice and ZDF rats (Sloop 2004 doi:10.1172/JCI20911): oligo is outside the tile's modality_groups and its clinical counterpart (ISIS/IONIS-GCGRRx) is not a member, so no admissible patient comparison

Larger 2016 second human GCGR loss-of-function case (doi:10.1530/EDM-16-0081): same system as the Mahvash track; its hyperaminoacidaemia post-dates Kazierad 2016 and changes no status, so it is carried in that track's confidence_note
Conarello 2007 high-fat / streptozotocin Gcgr-/- study and Longuet 2008 fasting study: the same knockout system, used as model_src inside the gcgr-ko-mouse track rather than as separate tracks
Volagidemab population PK/PD in healthy Chinese and US subjects (2026, doi:10.1007/s11095-026-04028-0): human-data exposure modelling with no efficacy or safety prediction compared against patients
Glucagon challenge in overweight cats with MK-3577 (Mott 2024): already tracked in the draft (gcgr-cat-glucagon-challenge)
Volagidemab T2D dose-escalation NCT02455011: no results posted or published, so nothing for any added track to compare against in T2D; the antibody comparisons remain imported from T1D
